title: Receptionist Task Checklist
summary: Official Front of House (FOH) Station Checklist for Receptionists at Jiang Nan Hotpot. Covers the complete 8-stage guest journey: Initial Greeting ("Ni Hao! Welcome to Jiang Nan!"), Guest Details & Waitlist Verification, Service & Menu Introduction (₱899 Weekday / ₱999 Weekend + 5% service charge, Hotpot-only rates ₱699/₱799, +₱200 Premium Meat upgrade, Allergen Bill Out endorsement), Promotions (Birthday 4-vs-5 paying guests & Senior/PWD 12% VAT deduction), Dining & Soup Rules (pork-based broths except Mushroom, max 2 soup flavors, up to 3 initial meat plates), Policies (2-hour limit, ₱1,000 leftover fee, Outside Food Waiver), Server Turnover script, and Guest Departure OR/Invoice receipt check.
keyTakeaways: I. Initial Greeting: Greet every guest warmly ("Ni Hao! Welcome to Jiang Nan! Is this your first time dining with us po?") and respond with "Welcome back po!" (returning) or "Welcome po!" (first-time).

II. Guest Verification & Waitlist: Confirm name, pax count, and payment method (Cash, Credit Card, Debit Card, or GCash). Check table availability with Server; if full, log on waitlist, state estimated wait time, hand menu, and monitor waiting guests.

III. Package Rates & Menu Intro: Always lead with Hotpot with Grill Package — ₱899/person on Weekdays (+5% service charge) and ₱999/person on Weekends (+5% service charge). State Hotpot-only rate ONLY if guest asks (Weekday Hotpot-only: ₱699 + ₱200 Grill; Weekend Hotpot-only: ₱799 + ₱200 Grill). Offer Premium Meat Selection upgrade at +₱200/person.

III.5 Allergen Endorsement: Ask Dine-In and Take-Out guests about food allergies/dietary restrictions, consult the approved Allergen Guide, and write specific allergen info directly on the Bill Out form for the Server.

IV. Birthday & Senior/PWD Promos: Exact Birthday Today = 4 paying guests + celebrant FREE; Birth Month = 5 paying guests + celebrant FREE (with valid ID). Senior Citizen/PWD = only the 12% VAT component is deducted because the rate is already an unlimited dining promotion.

V. Soup & Initial Ordering Rules: All soup bases are pork-based EXCEPT Mushroom Soup. Guests may choose up to two (2) soup flavors per table and start with up to three (3) plates of meat for the initial order (unlimited desserts/beverages included; reorders via Additional Order Form).
VI. Dining Guidelines: Up to two (2) hours dining time; No Leftover Policy with ₱1,000 charge for excessive leftovers; Outside food allowed ONLY if guest signs the Updated Outside Food Waiver Form.

VII & VIII. Server Turnover & Departure: Escort guest when table is ready and endorse to Server ("Table ___ po, [number] pax, [hotpot/grill], with/without allergen or special request"). Upon exit, courteously verify and stamp the guest OR/Invoice receipt and bid farewell ("Xie xie! Thank you for dining with us at Jiang Nan Hotpot! See us again!").

quickRules.rule: Lead with Hotpot + Grill Package: ₱899/pax Weekdays (+5% SC) | ₱999/pax Weekends (+5% SC). State Hotpot-only (₱699 Wkday / ₱799 Wkend) ONLY if asked. Premium Meat upgrade is +₱200/pax.

quickRules.rule: All soup bases are PORK-BASED except Mushroom Soup (max 2 flavors/table). Always ask for allergies and write specific allergen info on the Bill Out form.

quickRules.title: Birthday & Senior/PWD Rules
quickRules.rule: Birthday: 4 paying guests on Exact Birthday OR 5 paying guests within Birth Month = Celebrant FREE (ID required). Senior/PWD: Only 12% VAT is deducted on unlimited promo rates.

quickRules.rule: Max 2 hours dining time; ₱1,000 fee for excessive leftovers; Outside food requires signed Updated Outside Food Waiver Form; Verify & stamp OR/Invoice at exit.

sections.title: I. Initial Greeting and Accommodation
sections.content: Task 1.1: Greet and acknowledge every guest warmly and politely; ask if this is their first visit.
bulletPoints: Standard Opening Script: "Ni Hao! Welcome to Jiang Nan! Is this your first time dining with us po?"
If NO (Returning Guest): "Welcome back po!"
If YES (First-Time Guest): "Welcome po!"

sections.title: II. Guest Details Verification
sections.content: Verify guest details, payment preferences, and table availability with the service team before seating or waitlisting.
bulletPoints: Task 2.1 (Confirm Guest Details & Payment): Confirm the guest's name, total number of diners, and preferred mode of payment.
Script (2.1): "May I have your name po and how many guests will be dining with us today? May I also ask for your preferred payment method? We accept cash, credit card, debit card, or GCash."
Check table availability with the assigned Server based on guest count and store capacity.
Task 2.2 (Waitlist Protocol): If no table is available, record the guest on the approved waitlist and provide an estimated waiting time.
Script (2.2): "May I have your name and number of pax po? Our estimated waiting time is around __ minutes. We'll let you know as soon as your table is ready."
Hand the menu to the guest, briefly explain the policy and reminders, and continuously monitor waiting guests.

sections.title: III. Service & Menu Introduction
sections.content: Tailor the service explanation based on whether the guest is a returning diner, first-time dine-in guest, or take-out customer, and document any allergies.
bulletPoints: Task 3.1 (Confirm Familiarity): Confirm whether the guest is a first-time or returning customer. If returning: "Welcome back po! Familiar na po kayo with our service or ordering process?" If NO / needs clarification: "Sure po, I'll briefly go over them with you."
Task 3.2 (Dine-In Package Rates): Clearly explain the Hotpot with Grill Package and state the applicable weekday or weekend rate, including the 5% service charge:
• Weekday Rate Script: "We offer our Hotpot with Grill package at ₱899 per person on weekdays, plus a 5% service charge."
• Weekend Rate Script: "We offer our Hotpot with Grill package at ₱999 per person on weekends, plus a 5% service charge."

• Hotpot-Only Rule: Always lead with the Hotpot with Grill Package. State the Hotpot-only rate ONLY if the guest asks — Weekdays: Hotpot from ₱599 to ₱699, Grill from ₱300 to ₱200 (Package stays ₱899); Weekends: Hotpot from ₱699 to ₱799, Grill from ₱300 to ₱200 (Package stays ₱999).

Task 3.2 (Take-Out Protocol): Present the Ala Carte Menu and confirm item availability before taking the order ("Here is our Ala Carte Menu po. Let me just check the availability of your selected items."). Confirm the order ("May I confirm your order po: 1 Meat Lovers Ala Carte.") and forward to the Cashier for processing ("Thank you po. I'll endorse your order to our Cashier for payment and processing.").

Task 3.3 (Premium Meat Selection Upgrade): For Dine-In, offer the Premium Meat Selection as an optional upgrade for an additional ₱200 per person ("Would you like to upgrade to our Premium Meat Selection for an additional ₱200 per person po?").

Task 3.4 (Package Verification): Verify the guest's selected package and briefly explain its inclusions ("Just to confirm po, you'll be availing our [selected package]. Let me briefly share what's included.").

Task 3.5 (Allergen Screening & Bill Out Endorsement): For Dine-In and Take-Out, ask whether any guest has food allergies or dietary restrictions and refer to the approved Allergen Information ("Before we proceed po, may I ask if anyone in your group has any food allergies or dietary restrictions? Let me check our Allergen Guide to assist you properly."). Write the specific allergen info on the Bill Out form so it is visible when endorsed to the server. Never provide unverified information.

sections.title: IV. Promotions & Special Occasions
sections.content: Proactively check for birthdays and Senior Citizen / PWD cards to explain mechanics accurately and endorse details on the Bill Out form.
bulletPoints: Task 4.1 (Birthday Promo): Check if the guest is celebrating a birthday or special occasion and explain the promo mechanics:

• Script: "Are we celebrating a birthday or any special occasion today po? For our birthday promo, if it's your exact birthday today, you only need 4 paying guests and the birthday celebrant eats for free. If it's within your birth month, you need 5 paying guests and the birthday celebrant is also free. We'll just need to verify a valid ID po."
• Verify eligibility and endorse the required information to the Bill Out form.

Task 4.2 (Senior Citizen & PWD Discount): Inform Senior Citizen and PWD cardholders of the applicable discount and explain that only the 12% VAT will be deducted, as the rate is already under an unlimited dining promotion:

• Script: "Do we have any Senior Citizen or PWD cardholders in the group po? Please note that only the 12% VAT component will be deducted from the total bill, as our rate already reflects an unlimited dining promotion. May I kindly check the valid card and ID for verification so we can note it for bill out? Thank you po."

sections.title: V. Dining & Ordering Information
sections.content: Explain soup base composition, maximum soup flavors per table, initial meat plate limits, and unlimited inclusions.
bulletPoints: Task 5.1 (Soup Selection): Explain the soup selection, noting that ALL soup bases are pork-based EXCEPT the Mushroom Soup, and that guests may choose up to two (2) soup flavors per table.
• Script (5.1): "For your soup base po, you may choose up to two (2) flavors per table. Please note that all of our soup bases are pork-based, except for the Mushroom Soup."

Task 5.2 (Initial Order & Reordering Rules): Explain the initial order and ordering rules — guests may start with up to three (3) plates of meat for the initial order, other menu items may be ordered per plate, and additional orders can be requested anytime using the Additional Order Form on the table.

• Script (5.2): "For your initial order po, you may choose up to three (3) plates of meat. Other items on the menu may be ordered per plate, and you can place additional orders anytime using the Additional Order Form on your table."
Task 5.3 (Other Selections): Advise guests that Ala Carte items are also available and that desserts and beverages are unlimited and included in the package.
• Script (5.3): "We also have Ala Carte items available if you'd like to order them separately po. Desserts and beverages are unlimited and already included in your package."

sections.title: VI. Dining Guidelines & Policies
sections.content: Communicate the 2-hour dining duration, the ₱1,000 excessive leftover charge, and the Outside Food Waiver requirement.
bulletPoints: Task 6.1 (Dining Time & Leftover Policy): Inform the guest that dining time is up to two (2) hours and explain the No Leftover Policy, including the ₱1,000 charge for any excessive leftovers.
• Script (6.1a): "Just a gentle reminder po, our dining time is up to two (2) hours. We also observe a No Leftover Policy, and any excessive leftovers will have a ₱1,000 charge."
Task 6.1 (Outside Food Waiver Policy): Inform the guest that outside food is allowed, provided they complete the Updated Outside Food Waiver Form before proceeding.
• Script (6.1b): "Outside food is allowed po; we will just ask you to fill out our Food Waiver Form before bringing it to the table."

sections.title: VII. Guest Turnover to Service Team
sections.content: Escort guests only after confirming the table is ready, and perform a complete verbal and written endorsement to the assigned Server.
bulletPoints: Task 7.1 (Table Readiness & Escort): Confirm that the assigned table is available and ready, then escort the guest to the table ("Your table is ready po. Please come this way.").
Task 7.2 (Endorsement to Assigned Server): Endorse the guest's information to the assigned Server so the guest is properly assisted:
• Script to Server: "Table ___ po, [number] pax, [hotpot/grill], with/without allergen or special request."
• Script to Customer: "Your Server will assist you with the rest of your order and dining needs po."

sections.title: VIII. Guest Departure
sections.content: Courteously verify and stamp the official receipt (OR/Invoice) prior to exit and deliver the signature Jiang Nan farewell.
bulletPoints: Task 8.1 (Receipt Verification & Stamping): Verify the guest's OR/Invoice (receipt) before exit and stamp the receipt accordingly.
• Script (8.1): "Thank you for dining with us po. May I kindly check your receipt or OR/Invoice before you go? Thank you po."
• Missing Receipt Handling: If the receipt is not available, courteously check with the Cashier first while maintaining a polite, non-accusatory approach.
Task 8.2 (Farewell Greeting): Thank the departing guest warmly:
• Script (8.2): "Xie xie! Thank you for dining with us at Jiang Nan Hotpot! See us again!"

title: Food Safety Act of 2013 (Republic Act No. 10611)
summary: Official Philippine statutory reference for Republic Act No. 10611 ("An Act to Strengthen the Food Safety Regulatory System in the Country to Protect Consumer Health and Facilitate Market Access of Local Foods and Food Products"). Establishes the legal obligations of Food Business Operators (FBOs), farm-to-fork HACCP & GMP standards, regulatory roles of DA, DOH-FDA, and DILG/LGUs, mandatory Food Safety Compliance Officer (FSCO) oversight, traceability, and statutory criminal/administrative penalties.
keyTakeaways: Primary Legal Responsibility (Sec. 13–14): Food Business Operators (FBOs) bear primary responsibility for ensuring that all food handled and served satisfies Philippine food safety law.

Farm-to-Fork Preventive Controls: Mandates science-based Risk Analysis, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Hygienic Practices (GHP), SSOPs, and Hazard Analysis & Critical Control Points (HACCP).

Tri-Agency Jurisdiction: DA (NMIS, BFAR, BPI) oversees raw/post-harvest meats, fish & crops; DOH (FDA) oversees processed & prepackaged foods; DILG & LGUs enforce PD 856 (Sanitation Code), Sanitary Permits, and Health Certificates.
Mandatory FSCO & Training (Sec. 28): Requires certified Food Safety Compliance Officers (FSCO) and mandatory food safety training programs for all restaurant and commissary personnel.
Traceability & Mandatory Recall: FBOs must maintain "One Step Back, One Step Forward" traceability and immediately withdraw/recall unsafe food while alerting regulatory authorities.

Statutory Penalties (Sec. 38): Fines ranging from ₱50,000 to ₱500,000, business permit suspension/revocation, establishment closure, and imprisonment up to 6 years for violations resulting in consumer illness or death.

quickRules.title: Primary FBO Liability (Sec. 13)
quickRules.rule: Restaurant management and food handlers are legally accountable for food safety at every stage from receiving and cold storage to table service.

quickRules.title: Mandatory Permits & FSCO
quickRules.rule: All branches must maintain valid LGU Sanitary Permits, Employee Health Certificates, NMIS/FDA-certified suppliers, and designated FSCO oversight.

quickRules.title: Criminal & Financial Sanctions (Sec. 38)
quickRules.rule: Serving adulterated or contaminated food carries fines up to ₱500,000, store closure, and up to 6 years imprisonment.

sections.title: 1. Declaration of Policy & Statutory Objectives (Articles I & II)
sections.content: Section 15, Article II of the 1987 Philippine Constitution declares that the State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people. Republic Act No. 10611 (signed August 23, 2013; Implementing Rules and Regulations Joint DA-DOH Administrative Order No. 2015-0007) establishes a comprehensive, science-based food safety regulatory regime.
bulletPoints: 1.1 Protection of Public Health: Protect the public from foodborne and waterborne illnesses and unsanitary, unwholesome, misbranded, or adulterated foods.
1.2 Consumer & Industry Confidence: Enhance industry and consumer confidence in the food regulatory system across primary production, commissary processing, warehousing, and restaurant food service.
1.3 Science-Based Standards: Promote fair trade and economic growth by grounding all food safety controls in risk analysis, Codex Alimentarius standards, and farm-to-fork traceability.

sections.title: 2. Key Statutory Definitions (Article II, Section 4)
sections.content: Essential legal definitions governing restaurant and commissary operations under RA 10611:
bulletPoints: 2.1 Food Business Operator (FBO): Any person, corporation, or entity (including Imperial Kitchen Group Inc. / Jiangnan Hotpot) undertaking to carry out any activity related to any stage of production, processing, storage, distribution, and preparation of food.
2.2 Food Safety: The assurance that food will not cause harm to the consumer when it is prepared or eaten according to its intended use.
2.3 Food Hygiene: The measures and conditions necessary to control hazards and to ensure fitness for human consumption of a foodstuff taking into account its intended use.
2.4 Food Safety Compliance Officer (FSCO): A trained and certified specialist designated by the FBO to oversee internal compliance, HACCP monitoring, hygiene audits, and regulatory coordination.

2.5 Adulterated Food: Food that contains any poisonous or deleterious substance, filthy or decomposed material, unapproved chemical/additive, or has been prepared, packed, or held under unsanitary conditions whereby it may have become contaminated.

2.6 Traceability: The ability to trace and follow a food, feed, food-producing animal, or substance intended to be incorporated into a food through all stages of production, processing, and distribution.

sections.title: 3. Basic Principles of Food Safety (Article III, Sections 6–12)
sections.content: RA 10611 mandates that all food safety standards and operational SOPs follow five core principles:
bulletPoints: 3.1 Food Chain / Farm-to-Fork Approach: Food safety is an integrated responsibility spanning raw material sourcing, transport cold chain, receiving inspection, storage, kitchen preparation, and dining service.

3.2 Science-Based Risk Analysis: Composed of Risk Assessment (scientific evaluation of biological, chemical, and physical hazards), Risk Management (selecting control measures & CCPs), and Risk Communication (allergen warnings, training, and alerts).
3.3 Preventive Measures (HACCP, GMP, GHP): Focus on preventing contamination before it occurs rather than relying solely on end-product testing.

3.4 Precautionary Principle: Where scientific uncertainty exists regarding potential harm to human health, provisional risk management measures (such as immediate quarantine and hold tags) must be taken immediately.
3.5 Transparency & Consumer Protection: Clear labeling, accurate menu disclosure, and prompt notification of public health risks.

sections.title: 4. Principal Responsibilities of Food Business Operators (Article IV, Sections 13–14)
sections.content: Under Section 13 and Section 14 of RA 10611, Food Business Operators (FBOs) hold primary legal accountability for the safety of food in their establishments:
bulletPoints: 4.1 Compliance with Food Law: Ensure that food satisfies the requirements of Philippine food law relevant to their activities and verify that such requirements are met through daily monitoring logs.
4.2 Food Safety Control Systems: Establish and implement Good Hygienic Practices (GHP), Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOP), and HACCP-based systems.

4.3 Traceability System ("One Step Back, One Step Forward"): Identify any supplier from whom they have been supplied with raw materials (Lot/Batch No., Delivery Date, NMIS/FDA certs) and track dispatches to branches.

4.4 Mandatory Withdrawal & Recall Duty: If an FBO considers or has reason to believe that food it has imported, produced, processed, or distributed is not in compliance with food safety requirements, it shall immediately initiate procedures to withdraw the food from the market and inform the competent regulatory authority.
4.5 Cooperation with Authorities: Allow unannounced entry of regulatory inspectors, provide requested temperature/sanitation records, and collaborate on risk reduction.

sections.title: 5. Philippine Food Safety Regulatory Agencies & Jurisdiction (Article V, Sections 15–19)
sections.content: RA 10611 delineates specific regulatory mandates across three primary executive departments and coordinates them through the Food Safety Regulation Coordinating Board (FSRCB):
bulletPoints: 5.1 Department of Agriculture (DA): Responsible for food safety in the primary production and post-harvest stages of food supply chains. Key agencies include the National Meat Inspection Service (NMIS) for fresh, chilled, and frozen meats; Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) for fish and seafood; and Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) for fresh vegetables and agricultural crops.

5.2 Department of Health (DOH): Responsible for the safety of processed and prepackaged foods, foods locally produced or imported under this category, and the conduct of epidemiological studies and disease outbreak investigations. Enforced primarily through the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Center for Food Regulation and Research (issuing LTO and CPR).

5.3 Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) & Local Government Units (LGUs): Responsible for supervising the enforcement of food safety and sanitary rules within territorial jurisdictions in collaboration with DA and DOH. LGUs enforce Presidential Decree No. 856 (Code on Sanitation of the Philippines) across restaurants, hotpot dining establishments, commissaries, markets, and food handlers (issuing Sanitary Permits and City/Municipal Health Certificates).

5.4 Food Safety Regulation Coordinating Board (FSRCB): Inter-agency body co-chaired by the DOH and DA Secretaries (with DILG, DOST, DTI, and industry representatives) that harmonizes standards and coordinates crisis management during foodborne outbreaks.

sections.title: 6. Training, Consumer Education & Official Inspections (Articles VI–VIII)
sections.content: Skills development and risk-based inspections are legally mandated under Sections 26 to 31 of the Act:
bulletPoints: 6.1 Mandatory Training of Food Handlers & FSCOs: All food business operators, food handlers, and supervisors must undergo mandatory and continuous training on safe food handling, hygiene, allergen control, and HACCP principles.

6.2 Role of Learning & Development (L&D): Internal training programs conducted by certified Food Safety Compliance Officers (FSCOs) fulfill the statutory mandate to ensure every kitchen and service staff member is qualified prior to deployment.

6.3 Risk-Based Official Controls: Regulatory inspections by LGU Sanitary Inspectors, FDA Officers, and NMIS Meat Control Officers are conducted regularly, without prior notice, based on risk classification and compliance history.

6.4 Foodborne Illness Surveillance & Retention Samples: Daily food retention samples (IKQA-SOP#011) and temperature/sanitation logs serve as vital forensic and legal documentation during DOH/LGU epidemiological investigations.

sections.title: 7. Prohibited Acts & Criminal/Administrative Penalties (Article XI, Sections 37–38)
sections.content: Section 37 defines unlawful acts under Philippine law, and Section 38 enforces severe financial, administrative, and criminal penalties:
bulletPoints: 7.1 Prohibited Acts (Sec. 37): (a) Producing, handling, or serving food that fails to comply with food safety standards; (b) Operating a food business without appropriate authorizations (LGU Sanitary Permit, FDA LTO/CPR, NMIS accreditation); (c) Failing to immediately recall unsafe food or concealing a food safety hazard; (d) Refusing access to regulatory inspectors during official controls; (e) Falsifying temperature logs, expiry dates, health certificates, or compliance records.

7.2 Graduated Monetary Fines & Permit Suspension (Sec. 38): Fines start at ₱50,000–₱100,000 (1st conviction + 1-month permit suspension), escalating to ₱100,000–₱200,000 (2nd conviction + 3-month suspension), and ₱200,000–₱300,000 (3rd conviction + 6-month suspension).

7.3 Hospitalization or Serious Consumer Illness: If the violation results in hospitalization of a guest, the penalty includes a fine of ₱200,000 to ₱300,000 and imprisonment of up to six (6) months, plus revocation of permits.

7.4 Death Resulting from Unsafe Food: If a food safety violation results in the death of a consumer, the penalty escalates to a fine of ₱300,000 to ₱500,000, imprisonment of six (6) months and one (1) day up to six (6) years, and permanent revocation of business permits and closure of the food establishment.

7.5 Corporate Officer & Employee Liability: If the offense is committed by a corporation, the penalty is imposed upon the responsible directors, officers, managers, or employees who participated in or permitted the violation through gross negligence.

sections.title: 1. Policy Statement
sections.content: Imperial Kitchen Group Inc., is committed to providing safe, wholesome, and high-quality food to our guests. We recognize that food safety is a shared responsibility and a fundamental pillar of our operations. We pledge to operate in full compliance with the Food Safety Act of 2013 (RA 10611) and all applicable local sanitary codes to protect public health and maintain the trust of the Filipino community.

sections.title: 2. Scope
sections.content: This policy applies to all aspects of our food chain, including procurement, receiving, storage, preparation, and service. It is binding for all employees (full-time and contractual), management, third-party contractors, and suppliers.

sections.title: 3. Responsibilities
sections.content: Cross-functional roles defined across company operations:
bulletPoints: 3.1 All Employees, Contractors, & Food Handlers: Must possess valid Health Certificates from City/Municipal Health Office. Must report foodborne illness symptoms (IKQAP#005) immediately. Must adhere to Personnel Hygiene (IKQAP#012) and practice continuous "Clean as you Go" (CLAYGO).

3.2 Supply Chain Management (SCM): Exclusively source raw materials and meat from NMIS-accredited and FDA-registered suppliers. Inspect deliveries for cold chain integrity and maintain batch documentation for rapid DOH/DA recalls.

3.3 Restaurant & Area Manager: Hold direct on-site accountability for daily food safety, refrigeration logs, danger zone thresholds, sanitation, pest exclusion, and chemical storage. Area Managers conduct unannounced regional audits.

3.4 Quality Assurance (QA): Custodian of compliance; updates Food Safety Policy and SOPs; conducts mandated quarterly internal food safety audits across all stores; investigates guest complaints and coordinates recalls.

3.5 Human Resources (HR): Enforces employee health documentation, verifies health certificates prior to store deployment, enforces Employee Health and Exclusion policy (IKQAP#005), and manages disciplinary actions.
3.6 Learning & Development (L&D): Designs and conducts food safety onboarding, refresher courses, annual retraining, and targeted intervention courses for stores with audit findings.

sections.title: 4. Principles
sections.content: Core pillars of food safety compliance:
bulletPoints: 4.1 Safe Sourcing: Only NMIS-accredited & FDA-registered suppliers. Inspection of all incoming goods for quality and temperature.
4.2 Personnel Health & Hygiene: Valid Health Certificate, zero tolerance for working with foodborne illness symptoms, hair restraints, clean uniforms, and handwashing.
4.3 Temperature & Time Control: High-risk foods must NEVER remain between 5°C and 60°C for >1 hour cumulative. Cold storage strictly at 4°C or below.
4.4 Environmental Sanitation & Pest Control: Proactive CLAYGO culture combined with rigorous Integrated Pest Management (IPM) using FDA-approved food-grade chemicals.
4.5 Traceability & Recall: Full records maintained for immediate trace and withdrawal in case of DOH or DA alerts.

sections.title: 5. Management Responsibility
sections.content: The management team is responsible for providing necessary resources, PPE, training, and sanitized facilities. The company commits to conducting at least one Internal Food Safety Audit in each store per quarter.

sections.title: 6. Non-Compliance Disciplinary Tiers
sections.content: Failure to adhere may result in progressive disciplinary action:
bulletPoints: 6.1 Minor Non-Compliance (Low-Risk / Isolated): E.g., single PPE lapse or minor temperature log delay. Corrective Action: On-the-spot rectification and informal coaching.

6.2 Major Non-Compliance (Repeated or High-Risk): E.g., failure to monitor CCPs or neglecting cross-contamination protocols. Corrective Action: Documented verbal warning and targeted refresher training.

6.3 Critical Non-Compliance (Gross Negligence / Immediate Threat): E.g., falsifying safety logs, serving known contaminated food, gross hygiene failure. Corrective Action: Immediate formal written warning, temporary reassignment, product disposal, and mandatory intensive retraining leading up to termination.

title: Thawing Policy
summary: Rigorous controls defining the ONLY 4 approved thawing methods (Refrigerated ≤5°C, Cold Running Water ≤21°C max 4h, Microwave for immediate cooking, Thawing as part of cooking). Explicitly prohibits room-temperature thawing and outlines rework protocols.
keyTakeaways: Room-temperature thawing (countertop, loading dock) is STRICTLY PROHIBITED.
Method 1: Refrigerated Thawing: In dedicated cooler at ≤5°C (41°F) on lowest shelves (2-3 days for large cuts).
Method 2: Cold Running Water: Submerged in original leak-proof packaging under potable water at ≤21°C (70°F) for max 4 hours cumulative.
Method 3: Microwave Thawing: Small portions only, followed immediately by conventional cooking.
Method 4: Thawing as Part of Cooking: Cook directly from frozen and verify the "Kill Step" internal temperature.
Mandatory Labeling: All items in thaw stage must have label: Item Name, Date Stored, Use By Date (48-72h).
Rework Protocols: Cross-contaminated items may be converted to "Cooked-Only" (min 74°C / 165°F kill step); solid beef sub-primals with minor contamination may undergo 1.5cm "Clean Trim".

quickRules.title: Only 4 Approved Methods
quickRules.rule: 1. Refrigerator ≤5°C; 2. Cold running water ≤21°C; 3. Microwave (cook immediately); 4. Cook directly.

quickRules.title: Thaw Shelf Placement

quickRules.title: Mandatory Label

sections.title: 1. Purpose & Principles of Safe Thawing
sections.content: To establish controls that ensure food safety and maintain product quality throughout the entire thawing process at Imperial Kitchen Group Inc. Bacteria multiply rapidly in the Danger Zone between 4°C (40°F) and 60°C (140°F). Leaving frozen food at room temperature is strictly prohibited.

sections.title: 2. The Four Approved Thawing Methods
sections.content: Only these 4 methods are legally authorized:
bulletPoints: 4.1 Refrigerated Thawing: Dedicated cooler maintained at ≤5°C (41°F). Must be on bottom shelves. Larger items take 2-3 days.
4.2 Cold Running Water Thawing: Submerged in original leak-proof pack under running potable water ≤21°C (70°F). Flow must agitate and overflow. Max 4 hours cumulative.
4.3 Microwave Thawing: Small portions only that are cooked immediately after cycle completes.
4.4 Thawing as Part of Cooking: For frozen burger patties, vegetables, or small seafood. Calibrated thermometer must verify the Kill Step.

sections.title: 3. Compliance, Monitoring & Labeling
sections.content: Thaw Log and Container Label requirements:
bulletPoints: Thaw Log: Record start timestamp, method used, and internal completion temperature.
Container Label: Must state Item Name, Date Stored, and "Use By" Date (typically 48–72 hours after complete thaw).

sections.title: 4. Corrective Actions & Rework Protocols
sections.content: Authorized reconditioning procedures under QA oversight:
bulletPoints: Conversion to "Cooked-Only" Status: If cross-contaminated by raw meat juices, redirect to a validated thermal kill step reaching ≥74°C (165°F). Strictly limited to biological hazards.
Rapid Chill & Repurpose: If discovered thawing in standing water at ≤5°C, pat dry, blast chill, label "Priority Use", and cook within 12 hours.
Clean Trim: For solid muscle beef sub-primals with surface contamination, a trained technician may excise the outer 1.5 cm with a sanitized knife. Prohibited for ground meat or vegetables.
Rework Authorization: Mandatory QA evaluation, Rework Log entry, and microbial swab test (E. coli/Salmonella).

title: Glass and Brittle Plastic Policy
summary: Eliminates foreign body physical contamination from glass, ceramic, and brittle plastics. Enforces zero personal glass in food zones, master glass register with shatterproof covers, and the 4-step Breakage Protocol with 3-meter quarantine radius.
keyTakeaways: Zero Personal Glass: Drinking glasses, mirrors, glass perfume/cologne bottles are strictly banned from food preparation zones.
Essential Operational Glass: Permitted gauges and windows must be recorded in the Master Glass Register and fitted with shatterproof films.

Glass & Brittle Plastic Breakage 4-Step Protocol:
1. Immediate Shutdown: Halt all food production in affected zone immediately.
2. Three-Meter Quarantine: Cordon off area with a strict 3-meter (10-ft) radius; all food and packaging inside this zone is treated as contaminated.
3. Segregated Cleanup: Use dedicated color-coded tools and deposit shards into labeled "Sharps" container.
4. Written Supervisor Clearance: Manager inspects and signs Breakage Incident & Cleanup Report (CAR) before work resumes.

keyTakeaways: Six-Step 40–60 Second Technique: Wet hands with potable water -> Apply liquid antimicrobial soap -> Rub vigorously for 20s+ (40–60s total procedure: backs, wrists, webbing, nails) -> Rinse thoroughly -> Dry with paper towel/air dryer -> Turn off tap using towel.

sections.title: 1. Purpose & Scope
sections.content: To mandate a scientifically validated hand hygiene methodology that serves as a primary barrier against the introduction and transmission of pathogens within the food handling environment. By standardizing mechanical and chemical actions, it eliminates transient microbial loads (enteric viruses and bacteria) and prevents human-vector contamination across all permanent and contractual employees.

sections.title: 2. Responsibilities
sections.content:
All Employees: Personally execute the 40–60 second handwashing protocol exactly as prescribed.
Restaurant Managers: Ensure structural integrity, continuous floor monitoring, and guaranteed 100% provisioning of antimicrobial soap, paper towels, and potable water.

sections.title: 3. The Six (6) Step Handwashing Method (40–60 Seconds)
sections.content:
Step 1 (Wet Hands): Use clean, running potable water.
Step 2 (Apply Soap): Use a generous amount of liquid antimicrobial soap (bar soap is strictly banned).
Step 3 (Scrub): Rub hands vigorously (total handwashing duration of 40–60 seconds). Scrub backs of hands, wrists, between fingers, and under fingernails.
Step 4 (Rinse): Rinse thoroughly under clean running water to remove all soap and loosened soil.
Step 5 (Dry): Use a single-use paper towel or high-velocity HEPA electric air dryer.
Step 6 (Turn Off Tap): Use a single-use paper towel to turn off the faucet and open doors to prevent re-contaminating clean hands.

sections.title: 4. Critical Control Points (Mandatory Handwashing Moments)
sections.content: Employees must wash hands immediately at these junctures:
bulletPoints: Before starting work or entering the establishment.
After using the restroom (Mandatory Double Wash Method: Wash in restroom, then wash again at kitchen station).
After coughing, sneezing, or blowing nose with a tissue.
After touching hair, face, wounds, or any part of the body.
After handling trash, chemicals, mop buckets, or cleaning tools.
After touching raw produce (especially unwashed root vegetables) before handling RTE sliced produce.
After busing dirty dining tables, handling used plates, glasses, or cutlery.
After taking a break, eating, or smoking/vaping.
After removing soiled gloves, before donning fresh gloves.

sections.title: 5. Corrective Actions & Contamination Assessment
sections.content:
Immediate Intervention: Manager removes non-compliant employee from food areas for just-in-time retraining.
Product Disposition: If an employee contacts a high-risk surface and touches food without washing, a contamination event is officially declared; all handled food is legally deemed adulterated and discarded immediately.
Surface Sanitization: All affected preparation surfaces and utensils must be stripped, washed, and sanitized before production resumes.

sections.title: 6. Facility Infrastructure & Multilingual Signage
sections.content: Sinks must be completely unobstructed with zero physical barriers. Prominent eye-level "Wash Hands" signage must be posted in all primary languages spoken by staff, supplemented by visual diagrams illustrating the 40–60 second scrubbing technique.

summary: Three-phase workforce competency framework (New Hire Induction, Role-Specific Technical Training, Annual Refresher). Establishes bifurcated assessments (written/digital quizzes + practical observation), the Talent and Capability Matrix, and sign-off archiving.
keyTakeaways: Three Training Phases: 1. New Hire Induction (orientation & food safety basics before active shifts); 2. Role-Specific Training (HACCP, equipment, POS); 3. Annual Refresher & Compliance.
Two-Pronged Competency Verification: Theoretical comprehension tested via quizzes + practical observation by supervisors on shift.
If It Is Not Documented, It Never Happened: Every session requires signed physical or digital sign-off sheets.
Talent & Capability Matrix: Centralized spreadsheet tracking who has been trained, skill gaps, and upcoming due dates.

title: Standard Operating Procedure: Crisis Management
summary: Rapid-response protocol for food safety emergencies (foodborne illness outbreaks, physical contamination, chemical hazards, or health office shutdowns). Outlines the Crisis Management Team hierarchy, 3 phases of management, Disciplinary Matrix with 30-day preventive suspensions, and 14-shift probation.
keyTakeaways: CMT Response Hierarchy: President/Owner (Crisis Director) -> VP (Deputy Director) -> FSCO/QA (Facilitator) -> Operations Manager, SCM Manager, Area Manager, L&D Manager.

Three Phases: Phase 1: Preparedness & HACCP; Phase 2: Crisis Response (immediate containment, evidence isolation "DO NOT USE", records securitization); Phase 3: Operational Recovery (CAPA, regulatory clearance, post-audit).
External Communications: No premature admissions of liability. All media and external statements routed exclusively through Communications Lead or President.
Regulatory Clearance: Full operational resumption is strictly prohibited until formal written clearance is issued by the sanitary inspector/health office.

Disciplinary Matrix: Minor Infraction -> Verbal/Written Reminders; Major Infraction -> Written Reprimand & 3-day suspension; Critical Infraction (willful endangerment, falsifying logs) -> 30-day preventive suspension pending termination.
Post-Incident: Non-compliant employees undergo retraining and a 14-shift supervised probation.

quickRules.title: Centralized Messaging
quickRules.rule: Never admit liability or speak to media. All inquiries go to the President/Crisis Director.

quickRules.title: Immediate Evidence Hold
quickRules.rule: Immediately tag suspected food and batches with "DO NOT USE" for third-party lab testing.

quickRules.title: 14-Shift Probation
quickRules.rule: Employees involved in safety violations must complete a 14-shift supervised probation.

sections.title: 1. Purpose & Scope
sections.content: Structured rapid-response framework prioritizing public health by containing food safety risks while ensuring compliance with DOH, FDA, and LGU reporting. sections.title: 2. Crisis Management Team (CMT) Hierarchy
sections.content:
President/Owner: Final executive authority on closures, public statements, and recalls.
Vice President: Strategic decisions and emergency resource allocation.
FSCO / QA: Internal traceability audit, regulatory liaison, NCR and CAPA.
Operations Manager: Large-scale operational halts, workflow adjustments.
Area Manager: Investigation, evidence collection, employee interviews.
SCM Manager: Supply chain quarantine and vendor traceability.
L&D Manager: Initial customer complaint intake and documentation.

sections.title: 3. Three-Phase Crisis Management Lifecycle
sections.content:
Phase 1 (Pre-Crisis): HACCP risk assessment, one-step-back traceability, supplier accreditation.
Phase 2 (Response): Operational suspension, evidence isolation ("DO NOT USE"), records securitization, regulatory notification, and centralized media messaging.
Phase 3 (Recovery): CAPA implementation, written regulatory clearance before reopening, post-incident review, and customer transparency.

title: Standard Operating Procedure: Personal Effects
summary: Controls restricting personal belongings, outside food, cosmetics, and jewelry in food zones. Enforces Bare Below the Elbows, bans false eyelashes and loose glitter, prohibits personal mobile phones on line, and mandates company-approved tumblers stored on lower designated shelves.
keyTakeaways: Locker Storage: All personal effects (money, coins, bags, e-cigarettes, nail clippers) must be locked in employee lockers before washing hands and entering kitchen.
Bare Below the Elbows: No watches, bracelets, or rings with stones (only plain, smooth wedding band permitted).
Cosmetic Standards: Light, blended makeup only. Water-resistant eye makeup. NO LOOSE GLITTER, SHIMMER, OR HEAVY POWDERS (risk of airborne migration).
False Eyelashes Strictly Banned: False lashes and eyelash extensions are strictly prohibited in all food preparation areas.
Fragrance Ban: Scented perfumes and lotions prohibited to prevent sensory taint of high-fat foods.
Mobile Phones: Personal cellphones are strictly banned in food prep and storage areas. Emergency calls taken in break area with apron removed.
Beverages: Hydration permitted only through company-approved tumblers with secured lids and straws placed on designated bottom shelves away from prep surfaces.
Contamination Event: If a personal item (phone, earring) falls into food, the affected food batch must be immediately condemned and discarded (IKQA-WI#005).

title: Standard Operating Procedure: Waste Management
summary: Compliant waste segregation and disposal under RA 9003 and RA 6969. Mandates segregation at source (biodegradable, non-biodegradable, recyclables, hazardous), pre-treatment of food production rejects (crushing/pulverizing + sanitizer), intellectual property protection (defacing Jiangnan branding on boxes), and DENR-accredited hauler protocols.
keyTakeaways: Regulatory Alignment: Full compliance with RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste) and RA 6969 (Toxic Substances & Hazardous Wastes).

Segregation at Source: Biodegradable (organic food scraps), Non-Biodegradable (black bags to LGU landfill), Recyclables (sold to certified scrap buyers), Hazardous (spent bulbs, used oils in drums to DENR agents).

Food Production Rejects Pre-Treatment: Substandard rejects sealed in clear plastic with "Red" (Rejected) sticker signed by Kitchen Captain; MUST BE CRUSHED/PULVERIZED AND TREATED WITH SANITIZER to prevent unauthorized human consumption.
Intellectual Property Protection: All discarded cardboard boxes, vacuum bags, and stickers bearing Jiang Nan Hotpot branding MUST BE DEFACED OR DESTROYED before disposal; brochures shredded.
Medical / First-Aid Waste: Dedicated labeled bins emptied daily into secondary containers.
Construction Debris: Contractor sole responsibility; payment withheld until site cleared according to DENR standards.

summary: Master 11-page SOP establishing hardware color-coding matrices (cutting boards, towels, meat serving plates), the 15-minute intake cold chain rule, chronological batching sequences, cooking line boundaries, and allergen segregation protocols across Warehouse, Commissary, and Stores.
keyTakeaways: Cutting Board Color Matrix: Red = Raw Meat; Yellow = Raw Poultry; Blue = Raw Seafood; Green = Produce; Brown = Dairy & Cooked Foods; White = Allergen-Free Orders ONLY.
Meat Serving Plates Color Coding: Red & Yellow = US Beef; Brown & Green = Pork Belly; Orange = Angus Beef.
Sanitation Towels: Blue = FOH Dining; Yellow = Handwash Sinks; Green = BOH Kitchen; White = Clean Wares; Red = Restroom ONLY.
Chronological Batching Sequence: Shift Start = Clean Run (allergen-free, RTE items, clean vegetables); Shift End = Raw/Allergen Run.
Cooking Line Boundary: Line of demarcation. Line cooks must use entirely separate dedicated tongs & plates for raw protein placement versus cooked protein retrieval.
Hygienic Reset: 40–60 second handwashing + fresh gloves when switching tasks or food groups.
Spill Response: Cordon off area immediately, deploy color-coded spill kit, wash/rinse/sanitize before resuming.

title: Standard Operating Procedure: Food Retention Sample
summary: Mandatory daily collection, labeling, storage, and disposal of food retention samples across all branches and commissary. Defines sampling portions (broths 100-150mL, meats 100g, sauces 100g, ice cream 100mL, service water 250mL, ice 100g), 5-7 days holding period at ≤4°C or ≤-18°C, and vacuum-sealed packaging.
keyTakeaways: Universal Compliance: Daily retention sampling is compulsory across all branches regardless of sales volume or guest traffic.

Mandatory Sampling Matrix: Soup/broths (100-150mL), Meats (100g per type), Sauces (100g per type), Sauce bar items (100g), Produce (100g), Ball items (100g / 2-4 pcs), Ice cream mix (100mL), Halo-halo mix (100mL), Service water (250mL), Edible ice (100g).
Packaging: Sterile, food-grade PE plastic bags, vacuum-sealed to prevent air exposure and leaks.
Storage Temperatures: Refrigerated items at ≤4°C; Frozen items at ≤-18°C in dedicated retention freezers.
Retention Period: Exactly 5 to 7 days from collection date and time.
Labeling Standard: Item Name, Date & Time Collected, Batch No, Collected By & signature, Retention End By, Manager on Duty (MOD) signature.
Disposal: After 5-7 days, logged in Daily Retention Monitoring and disposed of as wastage; NEVER consumed, reused, or returned to service.

quickRules.title: 5-7 Days Retention Period
quickRules.rule: Hold all daily samples under controlled cold storage for 5 to 7 days before disposal.

quickRules.title: Dedicated Retention Freezer
quickRules.rule: Retention samples must be stored in dedicated freezers (≤-18°C) or chillers (≤4°C).

quickRules.title: Never Consume Samples
quickRules.rule: Expired retention samples must be discarded as waste; never consumed or reused.

keyTakeaways: Wire Slicer Inspection: Inspect wire slicer prior to use; report damaged, slack, or frayed slicing wires immediately.
Personal Hygiene & Gloves: Don clean food-grade disposable gloves prior to touching luncheon meat or slicer food contact surfaces.
Uniform Slice Presentation: Safely operate wire slicer to cut luncheon meat uniformly, maintaining portion control and hotpot visual plating standards.
Sanitation & Storage: Slicers and preparation utensils must be thoroughly washed, rinsed, sanitized, and stored after each shift.
Supervisory Oversight: Kitchen Captain inspects portion accuracy, plate aesthetics, and equipment condition daily.

sections.title: 1. Purpose & Scope
sections.content: To establish a standardized procedure for safe, hygienic, uniform cutting and portioning of luncheon meat using a wire slicer to ensure product consistency, visual presentation standards, portion control, and food safety compliance across kitchen employees, prep staff, and shift leaders.

sections.title: 2. Responsibilities
sections.content:
Kitchen Employees: Wear clean food-grade gloves, safely operate wire slicer, portion and plate uniformly, report damaged slicers.
Kitchen Captain: Directly supervise daily prep, inspect portion accuracy and visual plating standards, verify slicer cleaning and sanitization after each shift.

sections.title: 3. Operational Procedures & Equipment Care
sections.content:
Pre-Operational Check: Verify wire tension and hygiene cleanliness.
Slicing & Portioning: Place chilled luncheon meat block firmly on base; depress wire frame in smooth single downward stroke to yield uniform slices.
Plating: Fan slices neatly according to Jiangnan presentation guidelines.
Sanitation: Strip food debris, wash with warm detergent, rinse, sanitize with approved food-contact sanitizer, and air dry.
